name: MonkeyOCRv2-Und (S 1.7B, B 1.8B)
vendor: HUST (Xiang Bai, Yuliang Liu groups; HF org zenosai)

lineage.how_derived: MonkeyOCRv2 document-native vision encoder (S 28M / B 113M) with a language model for document understanding (question answering)

purpose: Efficient document understanding (questions about documents, charts, tables) built on the MonkeyOCRv2 encoder; the paper reports it beats CLIP-, DINO- and SAM-based encoders on eight benchmarks under identical training settings (arXiv 2607.11562 abstract).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (code and all weights); MonkeyDoc v2 annotations CC BY 4.0
license.notes: GitHub LICENSE file read: "The code and all MonkeyOCRv2 model weights (encoders, Parsing, Und) are released under the Apache License 2.0 ... MonkeyDoc v2 annotations are released under CC BY 4.0; see the dataset card for image-source terms." The file is this short grant, not the full Apache text (GitHub reports license metadata NOASSERTION); the HF card tag and card text agree ("free for both research and commercial use"). The HF repos carry no LICENSE file.

architecture.kind: vision-language: MonkeyOCRv2 ViT encoder plus a language model (card gives only total sizes 1.7B / 1.8B and does not name the LLM)

benchmarks.name: OCRBench
benchmarks.variant: B-Und (S-Und 52.2); the card scale is 0-100, not the 0-1000 scale used by Qwen

strengths: small document QA model with a document-native encoder
weaknesses: numbers far below Qwen3-VL-8B (DocVQA 96.1, InfoVQA 83.1 vendor) and Qwen3.5: a research model for the encoder, not a competitive reader
almost no downloads or community use
soft.maturity: released with the parsing models in July 2026; no reports found

tona_fit.reason: document-QA quality is well below the general VLMs we already track (Qwen3-VL-8B DocVQA 96.1 vs 79.3 here); the parsing sibling is the useful release
blockers: Tona engine has no vision architecture
